prompt.context: The federal government of a country is investigating whether to restart a rubber factory in the western part of the country. The factory was operational in the past but has not been used for 7 years. The plant was closed due to terrorism in the area, which has now come down significantly though there are still issues and skirmishes reported. If rejuvenated, the plant may become a target for rebels. All the equipment is considered useable but the government still estimates spending $12M to rejuvenate the plant, which would enable the plant to produce up to 10M lbs of rubber per month. The demand for rubber worldwide is strong but rubber must be transported to an export port via trains; up to 2 trains per day can be used for this.
prompt.question: Should the government proceed with this investment? Calculate the ROI and identify key risks and benefits.

clarifying_info.q: What are the raw materials needed?
clarifying_info.a: Gum resin is needed. 3 lbs of resin after processing results in 1 lb of rubber.

clarifying_info.q: Where does the resin come from?
clarifying_info.a: Resin must be transported from the capital. Up to 4 trains per day can be used for this (this is a key question — a candidate not asking misses a key element).

clarifying_info.q: What price can rubber be sold at?
clarifying_info.a: Rubber sells at $20 per lb. Gum resin costs $5 per lb.
The rubber would be sold in the commodity market to the entire world.
Market demand is strong; assume whatever the plant produces can be sold.

framework: Analyze financial benefits of the investment: ROI, revenue, costs

Analyze production capacity: equipment capacity is 10M lbs/month but actual output is likely constrained by supply and distribution — map the full value chain (Resin Supplier → Plant → Customers) to identify bottlenecks
Identify other government-specific benefits: employment creation, economic development of the region
Identify and assess risks: terrorism, labor shortage, single supplier, transportation dependency, thin margins
Deliver a recommendation with numbers, risks, and next steps

questions.prompt: Calculate the outgoing train capacity (rubber export). Assume 25 working days per month.
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply: trains/day × bogies/train × cases/bogie × lbs/case × days/month. The result caps how much rubber can be exported regardless of plant capacity.

math.setup: Outgoing trains: 2 trains/day, 8 bogies/train, 25 cases/bogie, 500 lbs/case, 25 days/month
math.answer: Outgoing capacity = 5,000,000 lbs of rubber per month

questions.prompt: Calculate the incoming train capacity (resin supply). Assume 25 working days per month.
questions.guidance: Candidate should perform the same structure for inbound trains carrying resin, then apply the 3:1 resin-to-rubber conversion to see how much rubber the inbound supply supports.

math.setup: Incoming trains: 4 trains/day, 10 bogies/train, 25 barrels/bogie, 640 lbs/barrel, 25 days/month
math.answer: Incoming resin supply supports ~5.33M lbs of rubber per month — slightly above outgoing capacity

questions.prompt: Identify the binding bottleneck. What limits actual production?
questions.guidance: Outgoing train capacity (5M lbs) is slightly below what the incoming resin supply supports (5.33M lbs) and well below the equipment ceiling (10M lbs). The bottleneck is outgoing transportation. Monthly production should be pegged at 5M lbs.

math.answer: Bottleneck is outgoing transport; effective monthly output = 5,000,000 lbs of rubber

questions.prompt: Build the monthly income statement and calculate ROI. Use: rubber price $20/lb, resin cost $5/lb (3 lbs resin per lb rubber), labor $8M/month, other fixed overhead $10M/month, train trip cost $40,000 (both inbound and outbound, assume all trains run daily).
questions.guidance: Revenue uses 5M lbs at $20. Material cost uses 15M lbs of resin at $5. Transportation cost uses all 6 daily trains (4 inbound + 2 outbound) × 25 days × $40,000. Then derive profit and ROI against $12M investment.

math.answer: Monthly profit = $1M; annual profit = $12M; payback period = 1 year; margin = 1%

questions.prompt: What other areas would you explore to support the government's recommendation?
questions.guidance: Candidate should discuss non-financial government benefits and risks with mitigations.

brainstorming.prompt: Beyond the financials, what risks and other benefits should the government consider before proceeding?

categories.name: Non-financial benefits
ideas: Employment creation — $8M/month labor cost signals a labor-intensive operation providing significant local jobs
Economic development of the western region
Infrastructure improvement (rail, roads) as a spillover benefit

categories.name: Price / margin risk
ideas: Margins are only 1% — highly exposed to resin price increases or rubber price drops
Mitigation: forward contracts to purchase resin at fixed prices
Mitigation: forward contracts to sell rubber at fixed prices

categories.name: Labor risk
ideas: Difficulty attracting workers to a region with ongoing terrorism
Mitigation: introduce automation to reduce labor dependency
Mitigation: facilitate migration of labor from other areas with incentives

categories.name: Terrorism risk
ideas: Plant could become a target for rebels once operational
Mitigation: involve community leaders in the process to build local support
Mitigation: arrange government or private security for the plant

categories.name: Supply chain / transportation risk
ideas: Sole dependency on trains for both inbound resin and outbound rubber
Mitigation: maintain adequate safety stock of resin and finished rubber
Mitigation: ensure rail tracks are protected in sensitive areas
Mitigation: diversify transport modes — invest in roads, pursue waterways if applicable

categories.name: Supplier concentration risk
ideas: Single identified resin supplier creates dependency

recommendation: Proceed with the investment — the plant is financially viable with a 1-year payback period and $12M annual profit
Production will be capped at 5M lbs/month by outgoing train capacity, not equipment; addressing this bottleneck would increase profits further
risks: 1% profit margin means the financials are fragile — small input cost increases or output price drops could eliminate profit
Terrorism risk poses operational and safety threat to staff and infrastructure
Single resin supplier and train-only logistics create supply chain fragility
next_steps: Assess how the plant can be staffed given regional security concerns
Investigate whether outgoing train capacity can be expanded (e.g., additional trains or alternative export routes) to unlock higher production
Evaluate terrorism threat level and specific mitigation measures (security, community engagement)
Negotiate forward contracts on resin and rubber to protect thin margins
Develop supplier diversification plan to reduce single-supplier risk
